1 Important Information for Tentative Rulings and Hearings:
2
1. Please review and follow the Tentative Ruling Instructions which can be found on the Court’s website
3
using the following link: https://sf.courts.ca.gov/divisions/unified-family-court/ufc-tentative-rulings.
4
2. If you wish to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case, you must notify the other party
5
(unless there is a restraining order in place) and the Court Clerk in the Department where the hearing
6
is scheduled of your objection by 4:00 PM the Court day prior to the hearing date. Court days do not
7
include Court holidays, Saturdays, or Sundays. The Court’s Holiday Schedule can be found on the
8
Court’s website using the following link: https://sf.courts.ca.gov/general-information/holiday-
9
schedules.
10
3. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 403 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
11
please call (415) 551–3741 or send an email to Department403@sftc.org.
12
4. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 404 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
13
please call (415) 551–3744 or send an email to Department404@sftc.org.
14
5. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 416 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
15
please call (415) 551– 3756 or send an email to Department416@sftc.org.
16
6. When you contact the Court Clerk to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case, please
17
specify the paragraph(s) and / or line number(s) of the Tentative Ruling which contains the language
18
to which you object.
19
7. You may appear at your hearing either (a) in-person; (b) by video; or (c) by phone. Pursuant to SFLR
20
11.7(D)(4), if you choose to appear by video or phone, you must be continuously connected to Zoom
21
from 8:50 a.m. until 12:00 p.m. or until your hearing is concluded (or from 1:20 p.m. until 4:30 p.m.
22
or until your hearing is concluded, if your hearing is scheduled to start at 1:30 p.m.). If you fail to
23
appear in-person, by video, or phone, the Court may proceed with the hearing in your absence. The
24
Court is not required to contact you before your hearing.
25
8. If you choose to appear by video or by phone, you must comply with the Notice and Instructions for
26
Remote Appearances in San Francisco Family Court set forth below.
27

12 REQUEST FOR ORDER FOR CHANGE OF TEMPORARY EMERGENCY ORDER, CHILD
13 CUSTODY, VISITATION (PARENTING TIME)
14 TENTATIVE RULING
15 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
16 Court makes the following findings and orders:
17 A. Procedural History
18 1) The parents subject to this proceeding are Respondent/Father, Sean M. Cottrell and Other
19 Parent/Mother, Estrele Capcha. The minor child subject to this proceeding is Kyle Reilly Capcha
20 Condori born on 04/03/19.
21 2) On October 27, 2025, Mother filed an Ex Parte application seeking sole legal and sole physical
22 custody of the minor child and that Father have parenting time on weekends from Friday after
23 school through Sunday at 1:00 p.m.
24 3) On October 27, 2025, Father filed a Responsive Declaration to Mother’s Ex Parte application in
25 which he asks the Court to order the following:
26 a. Deny mother’s requests;
27 b. Maintain the existing custody orders that Father have sole legal and sole physical
28 custody.
29
1 c. Modify the existing parenting plan, such that Mother has parenting time every other
2 Sunday from 10:00 a.m. – 6:00 p.m.
3 d. Change the child’s name. However, it should be noted that the Court previously granted
4 this request (see FOAH filed 11/03/25).
5 4) The Court denied Mother’s requests, pending hearing.
6 5) On November 18, 2025, Father filed another Responsive Declaration in which he is now
7 requesting that Mother have supervised visitation for 3 months and then every Sunday from 10:00
8 a.m – 6:00 p.m. He is requesting to have the second and fifth weekends with the minor child.
9 6) On December 3, 2025, the Court set the matter for FCS Mediation on 01/08/26 and set the matter
10 for return on 02/10/26 at 9:00 a.m., in Department 403.
11 7) On January 26, 2026, Father filed another Responsive Declaration, which has been read and
12 considered by this Court.
13 B. Findings and Order
14 1) This Court has jurisdiction to make child custody orders in this case under the Uniform Child
15 Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act. A violation of this order may subject the party in
16 violation to civil or criminal penalties, or both. The country of habitual residence of the minor
17 child is the United States.
18 2) Mother’s parenting time shall be modified, effective 02/10/26. Mother’s parenting time shall be
19 on the 1st and 3rd weekends of each month. The visits shall occur on Saturdays and Sundays from
20 10:00 a.m. – 7:00 p.m.
21 3) Mother’s overnight visitation with the minor child shall cease immediately. Mother’s visitation
22 no longer needs to occur at Maternal Grandmother’s home.
23 4) Mother shall pick up and drop off the minor child at Father’s home. During Mother’s parenting
24 time is no longer confined to San Francisco County. She may travel with the minor child
25 anywhere in California, as long as she returns the child to Father by 7:00 p.m., on each of her
26 parenting days.
27 5) During Mother’s parenting time, Mother shall ensure that the minor child attends ALL of his
28 scheduled activities (school or extracurricular) that occur on her time.
29 6) All existing orders, not in conflict, shall remain in full force and effect.
1 7) The Court will prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing.

12 REQUEST FOR ORDER OF CHILD CUSTODY, VISITATION (PARENTING TIME), MINOR
13 CHILD'S SCHOOL DECISION
14 TENTATIVE RULING
15 The parties are ordered to appear. The parties may appear in person in Dept. 403 or remotely by
16 Zoom video. If a party chooses to appear by video, that party must abide by the Notice and
17 Instructions for Remote Appearances in San Francisco Family Court set forth above.
18 A. Procedural History
19 1) On October 22, 2025, Petitioner/Father filed a Request for Order seeking a initial custody,
20 visitation, and child school decision orders. The minor child subject to this proceeding named
21 Leela E. Dubois (06/24/16). The matter calendared for “readiness” on November 24, 2025.
22 Father’s request seeks:
23 a. Joint Legal and Joint Physical Custody Orders;
24 b. A 3-4-4-3 parenting plan; and
25 c. Orders that minor child remain in school in San Francisco School District.
26 2) On November 19, 2025, Respondent/Mother filed a Responsive Declaration to Father’s Request
27 for Order asking this Court to:
28 a. Mother to have parenting time Sunday at 11:00 a.m. – Thursday to school;
29 b. Minor child to be enrolled in Berkeley Unified School District in Fall of 2026; and
1 c. Joint Legal and Joint Physical custody orders.
2 3) On November 24, 2025, the Court set the matter for FCS Mediation on December 29, 2025 and
3 set the return hearing on Father’s Request for Order on February 10, 2026.
4 4) On December 30, 2025, the parties entered into a partial stipulation, which provides as follows:
5 a. Joint Legal and Joint Physical Custody of the minor child; and
6 b. An agreement that the minor child be enrolled in individual therapy.
7 5) On January 23, 2026, Father filed a response to Mother’s responsive declaration, which has been
8 read and considered by the Court.
9 6) On January 28, 2026, Mother filed a reply to Father’s additional response, which has been read
10 and considered by the Court.
11 7) Both parents are still in disagreement on which school district the minor child will attend at the
12 start of the 2026-2027 academic year. Mother would still like to relocate with the minor child to
13 Berkeley.
14 B. Findings and Order
15 1) The parties are ordered to appear to set the move-away and school choice issues for trial. The
16 parties shall be prepared to discuss their time estimate for trial (i.e., number of days) and inform
17 the Court of the number of witnesses they intend to present.

12 REQUEST FOR ORDER FOR CHANGE OF VISITATION (PARENTING TIME), CHILD SUPPORT
13 TENTATIVE RULING
14 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
15 Court makes the following findings and orders:
16 A. Procedural History
17 1) The parties are Petitioner Maria Theresa Powers (Mother) and Respondent Andrew Daniel
18 Jenkins (Father). They share two minor children: Maxilliam (DOB: 5/28/14) and Lillian (DOB:
19 12/16/16).
20 2) After hearing on 8/15/24, the Court issued a guideline child support order of $758 monthly
21 payable to Mother with mandatory child support add-ons shared equally and extracurriculars add-
22 ons such as private school tuition requiring meet and confer.
23 3) On 10/23/25, Father filed a Request for Order seeking modification of parenting time and child
24 support.
25 4) On 10/23/25, Father filed an Income and Expense Declaration.
26 5) On 11/18/25, Mother filed a Responsive Declaration requesting Family Court Services (FCS)
27 mediation to establish a new parenting time schedule and consenting to guideline child support.
28 6) On 11/18/25, Mother filed an Income and Expense Declaration.
29
1 7) On 12/10/25, the parties filed a Stipulation and Order regarding a new parenting time schedule.
2 The parties agreed to the following:
3 a. Sole legal custody to Mother;
4 b. Joint physical custody;
5 c. Commencing 12/17/25, Mother shall have parenting time every Wednesday at 7:30pm to
6 Sunday at 10am;
7 d. Commencing 12/21/25, Father shall have parenting time every Sunday at 10am to
8 Wednesday at 7:30pm;
9 e. Mother shall have a vacation with the minor children from 12/26/25 to 1/1/26;
10 f. On 12/13/25, Mother shall have Lily from the time her play ends to 5:30pm;
11 g. Transportation: Father shall provide transportation to exchanges;
12 h. The parties shall communicate via text message and emails regarding any issues
13 pertaining to the minors; and
14 i. Per mutual agreement the parties may adjust the schedule to meet the needs of the minor
15 children.
16 8) Neither party filed additional pleadings.
17 B. Findings and Order
18 1) This Court has jurisdiction to make child custody orders in this case under the Uniform Child
19 Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act. A violation of this order may subject the party in
20 violation to civil or criminal penalties, or both. The country of habitual residence of the minor
21 child(ren) is the United States.
22 2) The Court confirms the Stipulation and Order entered on 12/10/25 is the operative parenting time
23 schedule.
24 3) Father’ s request for modification of child support is GRANTED as a modification of parenting
25 time is a material change in circumstances that justifies modification of child support.
26 4) Effective 2/10/26, and in accordance with the XSpouse report attached hereto and incorporated
27 herein, Father owes to Mother $475 in guideline monthly child support by the 1st of every month.
28
29
1 5) The Court finds Father overpaid Mother $283 in child support for February 2026. Father is
2 permitted to subtract $47 in monthly child support for the next 6 months (i.e., until the $283
3 balance is repaid in full).
4 6) The XSpouse reports are based on the following findings:
5 a. Per Father’s Income and Expense Declaration filed 10/23/25:
6 i. Father earns an average monthly income of $7,020 ($1,620 per week).
7 b. Per Mother’s Income and Expense Declaration filed 11/18/25:
8 i. Mother earns an average monthly income of $4,257.
9 ii. Mother pays $408 in monthly health insurance premiums.
10 iii. Mother pays $207 in monthly property tax expenses and $213 in deductible
11 interest expense.
12 7) All prior orders not in conflict with this order shall remain in full force and effect, including, but
13 not limited to, the Court’s 8/15/24 orders regarding child support add-ons.
14 8) The Court will prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing.

13 ENFORCING PERMARITAL AGREEMENT
14 TENTATIVE RULING
15 The parties are ordered to appear. The parties may appear in person in Dept. 403 or remotely by
16 Zoom video. If a party chooses to appear by video, that party must abide by the Notice and
17 Instructions for Remote Appearances in San Francisco Family Court set forth above.
18 I. Child Custody and Visitation
19 1) The parties are Petitioner Sylvanna Gavia Brennan (Mother) and Respondent Matthew Brennan
20 (Father). They minor children subject to this proceeding are Malachi (DOB: 6/5/2009), Gabriel
21 (DOB: 2/5/2012), Gideon (DOB: 9/24/2014), and Micah (DOB: 3/27/2017).
22 2) On November 22, 2024, a Restraining Order After Hearing was issued for the protection of
23 Mother and the parties’ children against Father. The restraining order expires on November 22,
24 2027.
25 3) On March 7, 2025, Father filed a Request for Order for Child Custody and Visitation seeking a
26 Family Code 3111 Custody Evaluation and a Family Code 3044 Rebuttal Hearing. Father
27 requests joint legal and physical custody of the children and equal parenting time.
28 4) Mother filed an opposition to Father’s motion on April 1, 2025. Mother states that the Father’s
29 Request for Order should be denied because a Domestic Violence Restraining Order was issued
1 against Father on November 22, 2024 for three years. Mother and the children are protected
2 parties under the terms of the Restraining Order After Hearing. Mother contends that Father has
3 not rebutted the presumption under Family Code section 3044.
4 5) On April 14, 2025, the parties appeared, and the Court referred them to Family Court Services to
5 participate in mediation. A new hearing date was set for July 15, 2025.
6 6) At the hearing on July 15, 2025, the Court denied Father’s request to change the custody orders to
7 joint legal and physical custody and declined to set a hearing to rebut the presumption under
8 Family Code section 3044. The Court ordered the parties to meet and confer on the issue of
9 minor’s counsel and the appointment of a child custody evaluator. The parties stipulated to the
10 appointment of Jill E. McInerny as minor’s counsel for the minor child Malachi Brennan. The
11 Court continued the matter to September 2, 2025 to review the need for a custody evaluator and
12 to hear from minors’ counsel.
13 7) On September 2, 2025, the court denied Father’s request for a child custody evaluation without
14 prejudice as it was deemed by the Court a premature request. The Court set a further review
15 hearing on October 7, 2025.
16 8) On October 7, 2025, the Court ordered Father to contact soberlink by October 10, 2025, so
17 Mother can receive daily reports. At the hearing it was noted that the Father had completed 40
18 weeks of Batterer Intervention. The court set a further review hearing on January 13, 2026.
19 9) On February 5, 2026, the parties filed a Stipulation and Order vacating the January 13, 2026
20 review hearing for custody and visitation.
21 10) As such, the Court finds there are no custody and visitation issues currently pending before the
22 Court.
23 II. Father’s 5/1/25 Request for Order
24 A. Procedural History
25 1) The parties married on 9/22/2001. Mother contends the parties separated on 5/19/2023, for a
26 marriage of 21 years and 7 months. Father did not list a date of separation in his Response to the
27 Petition filed 12/1/2023 and Amended Response to the Petition filed 12/8/2023.
28
29
1 2) On 5/1/2025, Father filed a Request for Order asking the Court to find that the Premarital
2 Agreement the parties executed on 9/21/2001 is valid and enforceable under Family Code section
3 1615.
4 3) On 7/22/2025, Mother filed a Responsive Declaration and Memorandum of Points and
5 Authorities asking that the Court bar Father’s ability to seek affirmative relief (including his
6 Request for Order filed 5/1/2025) “until he comes into compliance with all current Court orders”
7 (Mother attached to her Responsive Declaration as “Exhibit A” a list of orders Father has
8 purportedly violated). In the alternative, Mother asks the Court to set an evidentiary hearing on
9 the validity of the Premarital Agreement which Mother contends is not enforceable. Mother also
10 asks the Court to set for evidentiary hearing the validity of deeds executed during marriage
11 (Mother did not provide further explanation regarding this issue).
12 4) At the prior 10/7/2025 hearing, the Court continued the matter to 1/13/2026.
13 5) On 1/2/2026, Mother filed an Update Declaration reiterating her position that that the Court
14 should bar Father’s ability to seek affirmative relief until he complies with all current Court
15 orders. In the alternative, Mother requests the Court set an evidentiary hearing on the validity of
16 the Premarital Agreement no earlier than January 2027.
17 6) On 1/5/2026, Father filed an Update Declaration requesting the long-cause hearing be set at the
18 earliest date possible. It is Father’s position that no hearing is required on the validity of the deeds
19 executed during marriage.
20 7) On 1/13/2026, the matter was continued to 2/10/2026.
21 B. Findings and Order
22 1) Mother’s request that the Court bar Father’s ability to seek a Court order deeming the Premarital
23 Agreement as valid and enforceable until he comes into compliance with all current Court orders
24 is denied. The validity of the Premarital Agreement is in dispute and needs to be resolved in this
25 case.
26 2) The parties are ordered to appear to set a long-cause hearing on the issue of validity of the
27 Premarital Agreement. The Court will also adjudicate “the validity of the deeds executed during
28 marriage” at the long-cause hearing. The parties shall be prepared to advise the Court of a time
29 estimate for trial and how many witnesses they intend to present.
1 II. Mother’s 7/21/15 Request for Order
2 A. Procedural History
3 1) On 7/21/2025, Mother filed a Request for Order and Memorandum of Points and Authorities
4 seeking the Court bar Father’s ability to seek affirmative relief due to Father’s non-compliance
5 with Court orders.
6 2) On 9/25/205, An agreement and Order to Reschedule Hearing was filed continuing the matter to
7 1/13/2026.
8 3) On 1/2/2026, Mother filed an Update Declaration reiterating her position that Father should be
9 barred from seeking affirmative relief until he is compliant with current Court orders. Mother lists
10 the orders with which she believes Father is noncompliant. Mother asserts that Father remains in
11 contempt and has disregarded the Court’s orders for over two years.
12 4) On 1/5/2026, Father filed an Update Declaration alleging that Mother’s Request for Order is a
13 delay tactic. Father states that he has new counsel and is working towards compliance, having
14 already resolved half of the issues listed by Mother in her 1/2/2026 Update Declaration.
15 5) On 1/13/2026, the matter was continued to 2/10/2026.
16 B. Findings and Order
17 1) The parties are ordered to appear, and Father shall be prepared to update the Court as to the
18 status of his compliance with the issues listed by Mother in her 1/2/2026 Update Declaration.

12 REQUEST FOR ORDER RE ENTRY OF QDROS AND IRA TRANSFER ORDER PER JUDGMENT
13 TENTATIVE RULING
14 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
15 Court makes the following findings and orders:
16 A. Procedural History
17 1) The parties are Petitioner David Paul Pollak and Respondent Annette Louise Hurst.
18 2) On 12/2/24, judgment was entered on reserved issues, which includes provisions for an IRA
19 transfer order (see section 6) and division of retirement accounts by Qualified Domestic Relations
20 Order (QDRO) (see section 7).
21 3) On 11/6/25, Respondent filed a Request for Order seeking entry of proposed QDROs and an IRA
22 transfer order pursuant to the terms of the 12/2/24 judgment on reserved issues. The matter is set
23 for hearing on 2/10/26.
24 4) On 11/18/25, Respondent lodged proposed orders with the Court.
25 5) On 11/6/25, Respondent filed a supportive declaration from the consulting attorney who prepared
26 the QDRO.
27 6) On 2/3/26, Respondent filed a Memorandum of Points and Authorities in support of her Request
28 for Order.
29 7) On 2/3/26, Respondent’s counsel filed a Reply Declaration reiterating Respondent’s position.
1 8) The Court notes that Respondent references Petitioner’s Responsive Declaration in her pleadings;
